There are many results and conjectures about it, again reviewed in Section 9. To make a long story short, we have the following corollary of Theorem 1.1.



Corollary 1.2 (= Corollary 9.3).



If sg>6s_{g}>6 for every gg, then any holomorphic VOA VV of central charge 24 and dimV1=0\dim V_{1}=0 has the same partition function of the monster VOA V♮V^{\natural} for every gg.





The validity of the assumption on the slope sgs_{g} is presently open, and we call it the “weak Harris-Morrison slope conjecture” 9.2, which is again discussed in Section 9. This is the input we need from the geometry of ℳ¯g\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g} to study (partition functions of) holomorphic VOAs.




Other applications of our Theorem 1.1 are about the space of Teichmüller modular forms (Section 10) and the Schottky problem (Section 11).




From a mathematical perspective, especially in view of Corollary 1.2, it is natural to ask if the partition function is a complete invariant of the vertex algebra, i.e. if one can reconstruct the vertex algebra out of the knowledge of 𝒵V,g\mathcal{Z}_{V,g} for every gg. From the physics perspective we are asking if one can recover the Segal functor and hence the CFT from the knowledge of the partition functions as argued in [FS87]. In this regard Segal wrote “Friedan has conjectured that a field theory UU is completely determined by its restriction to closed surfaces.…This seems plausible but I don’t know the proof”, see [Segal, page 457]. Let us spell out this problem as a conjecture.



Conjecture 1.3 (Reconstruction Conjecture).



Let UU, VV be two self-dual VOAs of CFT type. If 𝒵U,g=𝒵V,g\mathcal{Z}_{U,g}=\mathcal{Z}_{V,g} for every gg, then UU and VV are isomorphic.
